content: A wife sought a 50% share of bank accounts and a home the husband claimed was an "indirect donation" from his father. The interpretative issue concerned whether proving the personal origin of funds suffices to exclude a property from the legal community. The Court applied a strict formalist principle: for real estate to be considered personal under Art. 179 CC, the personal nature of the funds must be declared in the purchase deed with the participation of the other spouse. Without this formal acknowledgement, the asset is common property regardless of who provided the money.
